summary: Blocker: Inaccurate return type description in `FutureValue.unapply` Scaladoc.

resolved_items.instruction: Revise the `@return` tag to: `@return `Some(Try[T])` if `a` is a `Future`, otherwise `None` (i.e., the raw `Option[Try[T]]` from pattern matching).`
Revise the first sentence to: `Extracts the value of a `Future` as `Some(Try[T])` if the `Awaitable` is a `Future`, otherwise `None`.
Revise the `@param` tag to: `@param a the `Awaitable` whose value is extracted if it is a `Future`.

disagreements.style_position: The `@return` tag claims the method returns `Some(Try[T])` if `a` is a `Future`, but the implementation returns the raw `Try[T]` from `f.value` directly, not wrapped in `Some`. The actual return type is `Option[Try[T]]`, where `Future` cases return `Some(Try[T])` and non-`Future` cases return `None`. The description conflates the `Option` wrapper with the `Try` value.
disagreements.rationale: The accuracy reviewer did not raise any issues, while the style reviewer correctly identified an inaccuracy in the return type description.
